claims.statement: The cloud relay is the gateway's optional push-style outbound bridge with three responsibilities — device registration, 60s heartbeat, and durable cloud-event upload — implemented in com.autonomousone.messages.gateway (RegistrationManager, HeartbeatManager, EventUploader) with all cloud HTTP funneling through the single BackendClient client; the durable gateway_event_outbox drained by EventUploader is the primary designed cloud event stream since v2.6.20 (PR-02), while WebhookEngine now handles only the user-configured local webhook (its fire-and-forget sms.received cloud leg was deleted); all components are supervised by ConnectionSupervisor alongside the LAN server and the GMweb pollers.

BackendClient performs JSON-only POST requests with 15s connect and 30s read timeouts, a User-Agent of AndroidGateway/<APP_VERSION>, and returns a sealed Result<T> (Success with body+status, or Failure with error, optional httpStatus, and isAuthError flag) so no exceptions leak to callers.

HTTPS is enforced at two layers for the cloud backend URL: GatewayPreferences.backendUrl's setter trims whitespace and trailing slash, allows empty (which clears the override), and requires https:// otherwise throwing IllegalArgumentException; and BackendClient.post re-checks prefs.backendUrl at request time and returns Failure("Insecure backend URL rejected — HTTPS required") without opening a connection, so the bearer token can never travel over plaintext HTTP.

The backend-facing docs (docs/api/README.md and openapi.yaml x-cloud-backend-contract) list exactly three app-to-backend endpoints: POST /api/gateways/register (no bearer token, optional X-Registration-Secret) with body {deviceId, name, appVersion, androidVersion, deviceModel}; POST /api/gateways/heartbeat (Bearer) with body {appVersion, batteryLevel, networkType, timestamp}; and POST /api/gateways/events/sms (Bearer) with body {eventId stable UUID, type sms.received, sender, message, timestamp} where eventId dedupes replays — all HTTPS. The app no longer calls /api/gateways/events/sms: v2.6.20 deleted the fire-and-forget cloud upload, and EventUploader's batch endpoint POST /api/v1/agent/events/batch is the live event-upload contract instead.

RegistrationManager.register() posts the device payload unauthenticated (authenticated=false so no bearer header is attached); deviceId is Settings.Secure.ANDROID_ID (unique per app signing key, reset on factory reset) with a fallback to a random 32-hex ID generated once and persisted as deviceFallbackId when ANDROID_ID is blank or unreadable, and name/deviceModel are 'MANUFACTURER MODEL'.

The optional registrationSecret pairing secret (Keystore-encrypted, user-savable from the cloud card via saveRegistrationSecret) is sent as the X-Registration-Secret header on POST /api/gateways/register only when non-blank, so the backend can reject unauthenticated registration attempts that would hijack or invalidate the gateway; clearing it in the UI logs that the backend must then allow open registration.

Registration is idempotent on the backend side keyed by deviceId: ensureRegistered() short-circuits to true when isRegistered and the token are present, and on token loss a re-registration issues a new token that invalidates the old one; register() blocks without consent, and on a 2xx response parses gatewayId and token from the body, persists both (token encrypted) and sets isRegistered=true, while a failure or parse error returns false without touching stored credentials.

HeartbeatManager sends a heartbeat every 60s (HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS = 60_000) with payload {appVersion, batteryLevel, networkType, timestamp}: batteryLevel is 0-100 percent or -1 on error, and networkType is 'mobile' when TelephonyManager data state is DATA_CONNECTED otherwise 'unknown' (Wi-Fi detection deliberately omitted as it would need an extra permission).

On heartbeat failure the manager sets state DISCONNECTED and sleeps an exponential backoff doubling from INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS 1s to a MAX_BACKOFF_MS 5-minute cap; success resets backoffMs to 1s, sets CONNECTED, and waits the 60s interval; both waits run as withTimeoutOrNull over a conflated wake Channel so they are interruptible.

BackendClient classifies HTTP 401/403 as Failure(isAuthError=true); when the heartbeat receives an auth error it calls prefs.clearCloudCredentials() (removing gatewayId, gatewayToken, isRegistered) and immediately calls registrationManager.register(), so a stale or lost token triggers automatic re-registration before the next heartbeat attempt.

HeartbeatManager.retryNow() resets the backoff ladder to 1s and sends a token into the conflated wake channel, canceling any in-flight backoff (or even the 60s interval) sleep; ConnectionSupervisor.retryNow() invokes it via the retryHeartbeat component callback when NetworkMonitor validates the network is online again, and the UI's manual Reconnect does too — without it a 5-second Wi-Fi re-association would wait out up to 5 minutes of the exponential ladder.

sendHeartbeat() first re-checks GatewayAccessPolicy.canTransmit(consent, isEnabled) and, if not registered or the token is blank, calls registrationManager.ensureRegistered() before POSTing; the start() loop also breaks to IDLE at the top of each iteration when consent is absent or the gateway is disabled, and the loop records lastHeartbeatAt on success.

HeartbeatManager exposes ConnectionState (IDLE, CONNECTING, CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, ERROR) via stateFlow, but the manager itself only assigns IDLE/CONNECTING/CONNECTED/DISCONNECTED — ERROR is set only by the UI layer (GatewayViewModel on a failed manual re-registration), and the GatewayViewModel derives its 'connected' chip from lastHeartbeatAt being within 90s plus isRegistered.

The backend URL resolves through a three-level chain: the GATEWAY_BACKEND_URL Gradle property (via ./gradlew -PGATEWAY_BACKEND_URL=... or gradle.properties) is written into BuildConfig.GATEWAY_BACKEND_URL in app/build.gradle.kts; when absent the default is https://gaitway.autonomousone.in; and GatewayPreferences.backendUrl returns the stored cloud_backend_url value if present, otherwise the BuildConfig default.

Nothing is sent to the cloud backend unless versioned consent is present (storedVersion >= CURRENT_CONSENT_VERSION, currently 1) AND the supervisor-derived runtime isEnabled flag is true — canTransmit gates the heartbeat loop top and sendHeartbeat and the local-webhook dispatch entry, the pollers gate on the same runtime flag, the uploader's in-loop gate is !isEnabled || gmwebUrl blank, registration blocks outright without consent, and GatewayService refuses ACTION_START without consent.

revokeGatewayConsent() removes the consent version and accepted-at timestamp, resets isEnabled, gatewayDesiredEnabled, and autoStartOnBoot to false, and calls clearCloudCredentials() (drops gatewayId, gatewayToken, isRegistered); the view model also stops the service, so revocation stops registration, heartbeat, and forwarding and prevents credentials from resurrecting traffic after reboot.

gatewayToken and registrationSecret are stored in SharedPreferences under the enc:v1: prefix via SecureStore (AES/GCM with a hardware-backed Android Keystore key), legacy plaintext values are transparently re-encrypted on first read, and persistence is fail-closed since v2.6.10 — storeEncrypted throws when the Keystore is unavailable rather than demoting to plaintext, so callers see an empty value until the Keystore recovers or the secret is re-issued.

The CloudConnectionCard and the other advanced transport cards (API Key card, Incoming SMS Webhook card) in GatewayScreen are compiled but currently hidden behind showAdvancedGatewayModes = false, with the GMweb pull bridge positioned as the recommended server connection; the effective cloud URL is still displayed by the REST endpoints card (cloud URL as base when connected, display fallback https://gaitway.autonomousone.in) and the foreground notification text carries 'Cloud: <backendUrl>'.

JVM unit tests covering the relay subsystem: GatewayAccessPolicyTest pins the canStart/canTransmit truth tables used at every cloud transmission boundary; GatewaySyncPolicyTest pins the outbox upload policy (100-event and 512-KiB batch caps, lone-oversized-event escape, full-jitter backoff bounds up to the 5-min cap); GatewayEventFactoryTest pins deterministic event/message identity, envelope round-trip, and cryptoVersion rejection; GatewaySyncSchemaTest guards the Room v6→v7 migration. The network-facing components (BackendClient, HeartbeatManager, RegistrationManager, EventUploader's HTTP path) remain Android-dependent with no JVM tests, are exercised on-device via the gateway screen log flow, and scripts/test-gateway-api.ps1 targets the LAN API rather than the cloud backend.

The inbound leg of the cloud relay has no app-side code that polls or receives relayed messages from the backend: an external project posts to the fixed backend URL and the backend forwards the message to the device's local GatewayServer, which serves POST /api/v1/sms/send (body {phone, message} plus optional subscription_id/smsc) authenticated by X-API-Key (Bearer Authorization header as fallback) with constant-time comparison and per-IP rate limiting; a successful send returns 202 (status 'accepted', handed to telephony) and a modem rejection returns 503 (status 'failed'), and this inbound path is managed by ConnectionSupervisor independently of cloud registration state.

Four alternatives to the cloud relay let external projects reach the same local GatewayServer directly without the relay backend, registration, or the GATEWAY_BACKEND_URL chain: Cloudflare Tunnel (cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8080), Tailscale (mesh VPN, no exposed ports), port forwarding + DDNS (router config), and ADB reverse (adb reverse tcp:8080 tcp:8080); the README positions the cloud backend as the zero-setup option, and these are pure transport choices over the LAN server so the consent and runtime isEnabled gates still apply.

The registration payload also enrolls device identity (PR-05, ADR-001): buildRegistrationPayload() adds protocolVersion 1 and publicKeys {trustRoot, signing, encryption} — Base64 raw uncompressed EC P-256 points from DeviceIdentity.ensureEnrolled(), which idempotently creates three non-exportable Android Keystore key pairs (StrongBox when available, else TEE); private material never leaves the Keystore, only public points are registered.

GatewayService.onCreate constructs EventUploader (service scope, shared BackendClient, logs into the service logFlow) and wires it into ConnectionSupervisor.ManagedComponents via startEventUploader/stopEventUploader; the supervisor starts it in the online-and-enabled reconcile branch and stops it on the disabled path and on shutdown(), while the offline branch sets prefs.isEnabled=false (stopping the heartbeat and pull poller explicitly), so the uploader's own runtime gate idles it with zero HTTP.

Cloud events are committed to gateway_event_outbox inside the same Room transaction as the message mutation they describe (TelephonySyncCoordinator: new-row upsert → MESSAGE_CREATED, delete → MESSAGE_DELETED, status refresh → MESSAGE_STATUS_CHANGED, mark-thread-read → THREAD_READ), so message and event live or die together and process death re-mirrors both from the provider; GatewayEventFactory derives a deterministic eventUuid from 'evt:<type>:<source>:<providerId>:<dateMs>' so the outbox unique eventUuid index dedupes rebuilds via INSERT OR IGNORE, and sender/body PII live inside the opaque payload envelope bytes (ciphertextB64+encoding+schemaVersion+cryptoVersion, cryptoVersion=0 plaintext JSON today, Phase 7 swaps AEAD bytes), never as envelope columns.

EventUploader's start() first calls repo.recoverSending() to flip rows stuck SENDING (process death between claim and ACK) back to PENDING before claiming; its loop then gates each iteration on !prefs.isEnabled || prefs.gmwebUrl.isBlank() (5s delay, zero HTTP), calls repo.claimBatch(now) — a Room transaction selecting due PENDING/SENDING rows with nextAttemptAt <= now, trimming to 100 events / 512 KiB, and atomically marking them SENDING — sleeps 2s on an empty claim, and POSTs the batch to /api/v1/agent/events/batch with each event as {eventId=eventUuid, type, conversationId, encoding, schemaVersion, cryptoVersion, payload} where payload is the envelope bytes verbatim base64-encoded (the server treats it as opaque).

EventUploader applies per-eventUuid partial ACK from the response's accepted[] array: a row whose eventUuid appears is moved SENDING → ACKED alone (repo.onAcked currently marks it with serverSequence 0 even though the response carries per-event serverSequence values), rows missing from accepted go back to PENDING via repo.onRetry with attemptCount+1 and their own full-jitter nextAttemptAt; a 4xx response other than 429 dead-letters the entire batch (repo.onDeadLetter, visible log line — never a silent drop), any other failure (transport error, 5xx, 429) requeues the whole batch and the loop waits full-jitter backoff (uniform in [0, min(5 min, 2000ms·2^attempt))) with the batch attempt counter capped at 20, and an undecodable payload envelope dead-letters that row only so the rest of the batch still ships.

Since v2.6.20 (PR-02) WebhookEngine is local-only: IncomingMessageDispatcher.dispatch() mirrors the message into Room via TelephonySyncCoordinator.mutate (which commits the cloud event in-transaction) and calls WebhookEngine.sendLocalWebhook fire-and-forget, which enforces GatewayAccessPolicy.canTransmit, requires a non-blank HTTPS webhook URL, and posts the best-effort sms_received payload with optional HMAC-SHA256 X-Signature — the fire-and-forget cloud sms.received upload no longer exists anywhere in the app code, and the durable outbox is the primary designed cloud event stream.

The legacy local idempotency cache in GatewayPreferences (hasEventBeenSent / markEventSent over a 500-ID insertion-ordered FIFO stored as cloud_sent_event_ids) is dead code with no remaining callers since the fire-and-forget cloud upload it served was deleted in v2.6.20; durable event deduplication now lives in the gateway_event_outbox unique eventUuid index.
